groups.title: Source-comparison queries Q1–Q13
groups.intro: Run in every validation run: the core benchmark (VCF-RDFizer v3.1.0), and the consumer WGS validation run and large-graph retrieval (v3.3.1). The oracle computes every expected answer in one pass over the source VCF with cyvcf2, using bcftools for exact FILTER text; both results are normalized and must agree exactly.

items.label: Q1 · Record density per 1 Mb window
items.summary: Counts how many variant records fall in each one-megabase window of each chromosome and checks that the graph gives exactly the same counts as the VCF.
items.pseudo:
reader = cyvcf2.VCF(vcf_path, strict_gt=True)
density = Counter()
for variant in reader:
    total_records += 1
    window_index = (int(variant.POS) - 1) // 1_000_000      # zero-based 1 Mb window
    density[(str(variant.CHROM), window_index)] += 1
expected = [{"chrom": chrom, "windowIndex": window, "recordCount": n}
            for (chrom, window), n in sorted(density.items())]
# normalize(): windowIndex/recordCount parsed with Decimal and accepted only if integral
# compare: rows keyed by (chrom, windowIndex), recordCount must be equal
# invariant (oracle and SPARQL side): sum(recordCount) == total_records
items.notes: Window index is zero-based (POS 1..1,000,000 is window 0) and CHROM is compared as its exact lexical string. The query computes FLOOR((POS-1)/1000000), which can come back as an xsd:decimal; normalize() parses it with Decimal and accepts it as long as it is integral.

sparql.label: common (both profiles)
sparql.text:
PREFIX vcfc: <https://w3id.org/vcf-core/vocab#>
PREFIX xsd:  <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>

SELECT ?chrom ?windowIndex (COUNT(DISTINCT ?record) AS ?recordCount)
WHERE {
  ?record a vcfc:VCFRecord ; vcfc:chrom ?chrom ; vcfc:pos ?pos .
  BIND(FLOOR((xsd:integer(?pos) - 1) / 1000000) AS ?windowIndex)
}
GROUP BY ?chrom ?windowIndex
ORDER BY ?chrom ?windowIndex

items.label: Q2 · Variant shape counts
items.summary: Sorts every record into a shape class (SNV, insertion, deletion, multi-allelic, symbolic, and so on) from its REF and ALT text and checks that the number of records per class matches the VCF.
items.pseudo:
for variant in cyvcf2.VCF(vcf_path, strict_gt=True):
    alt = ",".join("." if a is None else str(a) for a in (variant.ALT or [None]))
    ref, alt = str(variant.REF).upper(), alt.upper()
    if alt == ".":                       shape = "NO_ALT"
    elif "," in alt:                     shape = "MULTIALLELIC"
    elif alt == "*" or "[" in alt or "]" in alt or (alt.startswith("<") and alt.endswith(">")):
                                         shape = "SYMBOLIC_OR_BREAKEND"
    elif not fullmatch("[ACGTN]+", ref) or not fullmatch("[ACGTN]+", alt): shape = "OTHER"
    elif len(ref) == len(alt) == 1:      shape = "SNV"
    elif len(ref) == len(alt):           shape = "MNV_OR_EQUAL_LENGTH_SUBSTITUTION"
    else: shape = "INSERTION_SHAPE" if len(ref) < len(alt) else "DELETION_SHAPE"
    shapes[shape] += 1
expected = [{"variantClass": s, "recordCount": n} for s, n in sorted(shapes.items())]
# invariant: sum(recordCount) == total_records
items.notes: The whole ALT column is classified, so a multi-allelic record is a single MULTIALLELIC row whatever its alleles are. The rules are applied in order, so a symbolic or breakend allele is never classed OTHER. Both sides upper-case REF and ALT, and N is allowed in the sequence classes.

sparql.label: common (both profiles)
sparql.text:
PREFIX vcfc: <https://w3id.org/vcf-core/vocab#>

SELECT ?variantClass (COUNT(DISTINCT ?record) AS ?recordCount)
WHERE {
  ?record a vcfc:VCFRecord ; vcfc:ref ?refLiteral ; vcfc:alt ?altLiteral .
  BIND(UCASE(STR(?refLiteral)) AS ?ref)
  BIND(UCASE(STR(?altLiteral)) AS ?alt)
  BIND(
    IF(?alt = ".", "NO_ALT",
      IF(CONTAINS(?alt, ","), "MULTIALLELIC",
        IF(
          ?alt = "*" || CONTAINS(?alt, "[") || CONTAINS(?alt, "]") ||
          (STRSTARTS(?alt, "<") && STRENDS(?alt, ">")),
          "SYMBOLIC_OR_BREAKEND",
          IF(
            !REGEX(?ref, "^[ACGTN]+$") || !REGEX(?alt, "^[ACGTN]+$"),
            "OTHER",
            IF(
              STRLEN(?ref) = 1 && STRLEN(?alt) = 1,
              "SNV",
              IF(
                STRLEN(?ref) = STRLEN(?alt),
                "MNV_OR_EQUAL_LENGTH_SUBSTITUTION",
                IF(STRLEN(?ref) < STRLEN(?alt), "INSERTION_SHAPE", "DELETION_SHAPE")
              )
            )
          )
        )
      )
    ) AS ?variantClass
  )
}
GROUP BY ?variantClass
ORDER BY ?variantClass

items.label: Q3 · Ti/Tv
items.summary: Counts the single-base substitutions (biallelic SNVs) and splits them into transitions (A↔G, C↔T) and transversions (all other base changes), checking all three counts against the VCF.
items.notes: Only records whose REF and whole ALT column are each one A/C/G/T base qualify, so multi-allelic records (ALT contains ','), N bases and REF == ALT are excluded. The query returns a single row, compared field by field.

sparql.label: common (both profiles)
sparql.text:
PREFIX vcfc: <https://w3id.org/vcf-core/vocab#>

SELECT
  (COUNT(DISTINCT ?record) AS ?biallelicSnvCount)
  (SUM(IF((?ref = "A" && ?alt = "G") || (?ref = "G" && ?alt = "A") || (?ref = "C" && ?alt = "T") || (?ref = "T" && ?alt = "C"), 1, 0)) AS ?transitionCount)
  (SUM(IF((?ref = "A" && ?alt = "G") || (?ref = "G" && ?alt = "A") || (?ref = "C" && ?alt = "T") || (?ref = "T" && ?alt = "C"), 0, 1)) AS ?transversionCount)
WHERE {
  ?record a vcfc:VCFRecord ; vcfc:ref ?refLiteral ; vcfc:alt ?altLiteral .
  BIND(UCASE(STR(?refLiteral)) AS ?ref)
  BIND(UCASE(STR(?altLiteral)) AS ?alt)
  FILTER(REGEX(?ref, "^[ACGT]$") && REGEX(?alt, "^[ACGT]$") && ?ref != ?alt)
}

items.label: Q4 · FILTER distribution
items.summary: Counts records for each exact FILTER value (PASS, the missing value '.', or each failure-code string) and checks that the counts match the VCF.
items.pseudo:
def filter_status(v): return "PASS" if v == "PASS" else "NOT_APPLIED" if v == "." else "FAILED"
use_bcftools = filter_oracle == "bcftools" or (filter_oracle == "auto" and which("bcftools"))
if use_bcftools:                                   # the default inside the container image
    values = run(["bcftools", "query", "-f", "%FILTER\n", vcf_path]).stdout.splitlines()
    filters = Counter((filter_status(v), v) for v in values)     # an empty value is an error
else:                                              # --filter-oracle cyvcf2
    for variant in reader:
        raw = ";".join(variant.FILTERS) if variant.FILTERS else str(variant).split("\t")[6]
        filters[(filter_status(raw), raw)] += 1
assert sum(filters.values()) == total_records
expected = [{"filterStatus": s, "filterLexical": v, "recordCount": n}
            for (s, v), n in sorted(filters.items())]
# invariant: sum(recordCount) == total_records
items.notes: PASS and the missing value '.' are kept apart: '.' is NOT_APPLIED and is never folded into PASS. The lexical value is compared exactly, so a multi-code FILTER such as 'q10;s50' is one row. The query reads vcfc:filter on the record's call through STR(), so a '.' typed vcfc:Null still reads as '.'. parser.json records which oracle ran as filterOracle ('bcftools' or 'cyvcf2-serialization').

sparql.label: common (both profiles)
sparql.text:
PREFIX vcfc: <https://w3id.org/vcf-core/vocab#>

SELECT ?filterStatus ?filterLexical (COUNT(DISTINCT ?record) AS ?recordCount)
WHERE {
  ?record a vcfc:VCFRecord ; vcfc:hasCall ?call .
  ?call vcfc:filter ?filterLiteral .
  BIND(STR(?filterLiteral) AS ?filterLexical)
  BIND(IF(?filterLexical = "PASS", "PASS", IF(?filterLexical = ".", "NOT_APPLIED", "FAILED")) AS ?filterStatus)
}
GROUP BY ?filterStatus ?filterLexical
ORDER BY ?filterStatus ?filterLexical

items.label: Q5 · Per-sample genotype classes
items.summary: For each sample, counts how many of its genotype calls are homozygous reference, heterozygous, homozygous alternate, haploid, missing and so on, and checks those counts against the VCF.
items.pseudo:
reader = cyvcf2.VCF(vcf_path, strict_gt=True); samples = list(reader.samples)
for variant in reader:
    has_gt = "GT" in format_keys(variant.FORMAT)
    alleles = [None] * len(samples)
    if samples and has_gt:   # cyvcf2 genotype = [a1, a2, ..., phased]: drop the flag, negative code -> None
        alleles = [tuple(None if a is None or a < 0 else a for a in g[:-1]) for g in variant.genotypes]
    for sample, call in zip(samples, alleles):
        if not has_gt:                 cls = "NO_GT_FIELD"
        elif not call or None in call: cls = "MISSING"
        elif len(call) == 1:           cls = "HAPLOID_REF" if call[0] == 0 else "HAPLOID_ALT"
        elif len(call) == 2:           cls = ("HOM_REF" if call[0] == 0 else "HOM_ALT") if call[0] == call[1] else "HET"
        else:                          cls = "OTHER_PLOIDY"
        genotypes[(sample, cls)] += 1
expected = [{"sampleId": s, "genotypeClass": c, "callCount": n} for (s, c), n in sorted(genotypes.items())]
items.notes: Phased and unphased calls are pooled: the oracle drops cyvcf2's phased flag and the query maps '|' to '/'. The comparison is required only when the VCF has samples and at least one record with a GT key; otherwise the status is NOT_APPLICABLE_VERIFIED_NO_SAMPLES_OR_GT, with the comparison kept as a diagnostic. The expanded query reads each SampleCall's FormatFieldValue whose IRI ends in /fmt/GT and counts distinct sample calls. The condensed query cuts each sample's GT out of the tab-separated GT FormatValueVector by vcfc:sampleIndex and counts distinct records.

sparql.label: expanded profile
sparql.text:
PREFIX vcfc: <https://w3id.org/vcf-core/vocab#>

SELECT ?sampleId ?genotypeClass (COUNT(DISTINCT ?sampleCall) AS ?callCount)
WHERE {
  ?sampleCall a vcfc:SampleCall ; vcfc:sampleId ?sampleId .
  OPTIONAL {
    ?sampleCall vcfc:hasFormatValue ?gtValueNode .
    FILTER(STRENDS(STR(?gtValueNode), "/fmt/GT"))
    ?gtValueNode vcfc:fieldValue ?gtLiteral .
  }
  BIND(IF(BOUND(?gtLiteral), REPLACE(STR(?gtLiteral), "[|]", "/"), "") AS ?gt)
  BIND(IF(!BOUND(?gtLiteral), "NO_GT_FIELD",
    IF(CONTAINS(?gt, "."), "MISSING",
      IF(REGEX(?gt, "^[0-9]+$"), IF(?gt = "0", "HAPLOID_REF", "HAPLOID_ALT"),
        IF(REGEX(?gt, "^[0-9]+/[0-9]+$"),
          IF(STRBEFORE(?gt, "/") = STRAFTER(?gt, "/"), IF(STRBEFORE(?gt, "/") = "0", "HOM_REF", "HOM_ALT"), "HET"),
          "OTHER_PLOIDY")))) AS ?genotypeClass)
}
GROUP BY ?sampleId ?genotypeClass
ORDER BY ?sampleId ?genotypeClass

sparql.label: condensed profile
sparql.text:
PREFIX vcfc: <https://w3id.org/vcf-core/vocab#>

SELECT ?sampleId ?genotypeClass (COUNT(DISTINCT ?record) AS ?callCount)
WHERE {
  ?file a vcfc:VCFFile ; vcfc:hasRecord ?record ; vcfc:hasSampleSet ?sampleSet .
  ?record a vcfc:VCFRecord ; vcfc:hasCall ?call .
  ?sampleSet vcfc:hasSample ?sample .
  ?sample vcfc:sampleName ?sampleId ; vcfc:sampleIndex ?sampleIndex .
  OPTIONAL {
    ?sample vcfc:sampleIndex ?sampleIndexForVector .
    ?call vcfc:hasCallMatrix ?matrix .
    ?matrix vcfc:appliesToSampleSet ?sampleSet ; vcfc:hasFormatValueVector ?gtVector .
    ?gtVector vcfc:declaredBy ?definition ; vcfc:encodedValues ?encoded .
    ?definition vcfc:fieldId "GT" .
    BIND(?sampleIndexForVector - 1 AS ?zeroIndex)
    BIND(REPLACE(STR(?encoded), CONCAT("^(?:[^\\t]*\\t){", STR(?zeroIndex), "}([^\\t]*).*$"), "$1") AS ?gtLiteral)
  }
  BIND(IF(BOUND(?gtLiteral), REPLACE(STR(?gtLiteral), "[|]", "/"), "") AS ?gt)
  BIND(IF(!BOUND(?gtLiteral), "NO_GT_FIELD",
    IF(CONTAINS(?gt, "."), "MISSING",
      IF(REGEX(?gt, "^[0-9]+$"), IF(?gt = "0", "HAPLOID_REF", "HAPLOID_ALT"),
        IF(REGEX(?gt, "^[0-9]+/[0-9]+$"),
          IF(STRBEFORE(?gt, "/") = STRAFTER(?gt, "/"), IF(STRBEFORE(?gt, "/") = "0", "HOM_REF", "HOM_ALT"), "HET"),
          "OTHER_PLOIDY")))) AS ?genotypeClass)
}
GROUP BY ?sampleId ?genotypeClass
ORDER BY ?sampleId ?genotypeClass

items.label: Q6 · AC/AN distribution
items.summary: For sites with a single alternate allele, recomputes the allele number (AN) and alternate allele count (AC) from the genotypes and checks how many sites have each (AN, AC) pair.
items.pseudo:
for variant in cyvcf2.VCF(vcf_path, strict_gt=True):
    alt = alt_lexical(variant)
    if alt == "." or "," in alt: continue                 # single-ALT sites only
    single_alt_records += 1
    if not has_gt: continue
    an = ac = 0
    for call in alleles:                                   # per sample, phased flag dropped (as in Q5)
        if call is None or None in call: continue          # any missing allele: skip the call
        if len(call) not in (1, 2) or any(a not in (0, 1) for a in call): continue
        an += len(call); ac += sum(call)
    if an:
        ac_an[(an, ac)] += 1; q06_eligible += 1
expected = [{"an": an, "ac": ac, "siteCount": n} for (an, ac), n in sorted(ac_an.items())]
# af = ac/an is added on both sides but not compared; invariants: sum(siteCount) <= single_alt_records (== q06_eligible on the oracle side), 0 <= ac <= an
items.notes: AC and AN are recomputed from GT, not read from the INFO AC/AN fields. Only single-ALT sites with at least one complete haploid or diploid call made of alleles 0 and 1 contribute; a call with a missing allele, another ploidy or an allele index above 1 is skipped. This matches the query's contributions (AN 1 for '^[01]$', 2 for '^[01]/[01]$'). Phased and unphased calls are pooled ('|' mapped to '/'). The same NOT_APPLICABLE rule as Q5 applies when there are no samples or no GT.

items.label: Q7 · File metadata
items.summary: Checks that the file-level ##fileformat, ##reference and ##source declarations in the graph are exactly the ones in the VCF header.
items.notes: The key match is case-insensitive and a repeated declaration keeps the first value. The header is read from the file text because htslib's normalised header injects lines, such as ##FILTER=<ID=PASS>, that the file does not contain.

items.label: Q8 · Header line census
items.summary: Counts the '##' header lines for each header key (INFO, FORMAT, contig and so on) and checks that the graph has the same number of header lines per key.
items.pseudo:
header_text = the leading '#' lines read from the file itself (not cyvcf2's raw_header)
keys = Counter()
for line in header_text.splitlines():
    if not line.startswith("##"): continue           # the #CHROM column line is not counted
    key, _, value = line[2:].partition("=")          # key = text before the first '='
    keys[key] += 1                                   # case preserved
expected = [{"headerKey": k, "lineCount": n} for k, n in sorted(keys.items())]
items.notes: Keys are compared exactly as written (case-sensitive), unlike Q7's case-insensitive lookup. The #CHROM line is excluded because the mapping emits no HeaderLine for it. Counting per key localizes a dropped declaration instead of only shifting one total.

items.label: Q9 · Predicate census
items.summary: Lists every property used in the graph and how many times it is used, and checks that list against what the VCF implies, so a missing, miscounted or unexpected property is caught.
items.pseudo:
p = parse_vcf(vcf)   # one pass also counts records R, samples S, '##' lines H, ID/FILTER parts, FORMAT keys/slots, INFO values, alleles
P = {hasRecord, chrom, pos, ref, recordIndex, hasCall, recordId, alt, qual, filter, infoRaw, filterStatus: R,
     hasHeaderLine, headerKey, lineIndex: H, headerValue: non-empty '##' values, formatRaw: records with FORMAT,
     fileFormat/referenceGenome/sourceSoftware/fileDate: 1 if declared else 0, representationProfile: 1, ...}
P += ID/FILTER decomposition (hasIdentifier, hasFilterCode, componentIndex, ...) and FORMAT keys (hasFormatKey, fieldIndex, declaredBy)
if S: P += sample set (hasSample, sampleName, sampleIndex: S, ...) + definitions for undeclared FORMAT keys
    if representation == "expanded": P += SampleCall/FormatFieldValue predicates (R*S, value slots), genotype + phase-set layer, FORMAT value items, typed FORMAT values
    else: P += hasCallMatrix, appliesToSampleSet (records with FORMAT keys), hasFormatValueVector, valueEncoding, encodedValues (key occurrences)
if header_representation == "structured": P += emitted_header_counters(## lines)
if info_representation == "structured": P += INFO values, typed values, undeclared-key definitions, value items, SV carriers
if info_representation == "structured" or representation == "expanded": P += allele layer
P = {k: n for k, n in P.items() if n}; P[rdf:type] = sum(expected class counts)
expected = [{"predicate": iri, "tripleCount": n} for iri, n in sorted(P.items())]
items.notes: Counts every triple per predicate, rdf:type included (expected to equal the sum of all class counts). Zero-count predicates are dropped from the expectation, so a predicate the VCF does not imply must be absent from the graph. Expectations are derived from the VCF and the emitters' documented shapes, never from the mapping rules, so a custom --rules mapping makes Q9-Q13 report-only (NOT_APPLICABLE_CUSTOM_MAPPING). The expected inventory depends on the sample profile (--representation expanded/condensed), --info-representation (structured/raw) and --header-representation (structured/basic). Header and data lines are read from the file text, not from cyvcf2's re-serialization. Tandem repeats, local alleles and base modifications are not counted yet, so a file using them fails Q9/Q10.
items.differences: The query is unchanged. v3.1.0's oracle does not count two layers that both versions' emitters write: phase sets (vcfc:PhaseSet, inPhaseSet, phaseSetId/Name/Ordinal/Quality, expanded profile) and the SV carriers (isImprecise/isNovel, svLength, svClaim, VariantEvent/eventType/inEvent, CIPOS/CIEND faldo:InRangePosition intervals, CILEN/CICN ConfidenceIntervals, gVCF ReferenceBlocks; structured INFO). Under v3.1.0 a VCF that carries them therefore fails Q9/Q10 even when the graph is right. This is the mismatch NG131FQA1I hit under v3.3.0, whose census oracle is identical to v3.1.0's. v3.3.1 counts them (commit 3994e94) and keys FALDO terms by their full IRI (_census_iri).

sparql.text:
PREFIX vcfc: <https://w3id.org/vcf-core/vocab#>

# Every predicate in the graph and how many triples use it.
#
# This is the completeness check. Comparing it against counts derived from the
# VCF catches three things at once: a predicate that is missing entirely, one

def emitted_record_counters(
    rows: list[list[str]],
    samples: list[str],
    *,
    version: Any,
    contig_ids: set[str],
    alt_declaration_ids: set[str],
    has_assembly_line: bool = False,
    info_numbers: dict[str, str],
    format_numbers: dict[str, str],
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Counters for the allele, INFO, value-item, SV and genotype families.

    ``rows`` are the raw tab-split VCF data columns. Everything is derived from
    those and from the version, exactly as the emitters derive it.
    """
    classes: Counter[str] = Counter()
    predicates: Counter[str] = Counter()
    # The allele layer is reported separately for the same reason the genotype
    # layer is: it is not owned by one representation axis. Structured INFO
    # needs it for the Number=A/R/G value items, and the expanded sample layer
    # needs it for vcfc:calledAllele, so expected_census merges it when either
    # asks. Everything the emitter writes inside its ``emit_alleles`` branch --
    # the contig and assembly links as well as the allele resources -- belongs
    # here, or the oracle and the emitter would disagree about raw INFO.
    allele_classes: Counter[str] = Counter()
    allele_predicates: Counter[str] = Counter()

    assembly_contig_ids: set[str] = set()
    reference_alleles = alt_alleles = 0
    value_items = value_item_alleles = tuple_items = 0
    # FORMAT value items are counted separately: the emitter decomposes them
    # only in the expanded per-sample representation, so expected_census merges
    # them for that profile alone, exactly as it does the genotype layer.
    format_items = format_item_alleles = format_tuple_items = 0
    format_item_predicates: Counter[str] = Counter()
    genotypes = genotype_calls = called_alleles = 0
    phase_set_counts: Counter[str] = Counter()

    for row in rows:
        chrom = row[0] if len(row) > 0 else ""
        ref = row[3] if len(row) > 3 else ""
        alt = row[4] if len(row) > 4 else ""
        info = row[7] if len(row) > 7 else ""

        # A bracketed CHROM names a breakpoint-assembly contig instead of a
        # declared reference sequence; the two are mutually exclusive.
        assembly_id = vocab.parse_bracketed_chrom(chrom)
        if assembly_id is not None:
            allele_predicates["chromAssemblyContig"] += 1
            if assembly_id not in assembly_contig_ids:
                assembly_contig_ids.add(assembly_id)
                allele_classes["AssemblyContig"] += 1
                allele_predicates["assemblyContigId"] += 1
                if has_assembly_line:
                    allele_predicates["declaredInAssembly"] += 1
        elif chrom in contig_ids:
            allele_predicates["chromosome"] += 1

        alleles = vocab.parse_alt_alleles(ref, alt)
        allele_uris = {allele.index for allele in alleles}
        alt_count = sum(1 for allele in alleles if allele.index >= 1)
        for allele in alleles:
            if allele.index == 0:
                reference_alleles += 1
            else:
                alt_alleles += 1
            if allele.symbolic_id and allele.symbolic_id in alt_declaration_ids:
                allele_predicates["declaredByAlt"] += 1
            if allele.symbolic_type:
                allele_predicates["svType"] += 1
            if allele.breakend is not None:
                allele_classes["Breakend"] += 1
                if allele.breakend.orientation is not None:
                    allele_predicates["breakendOrientation"] += 1
                if allele.breakend.replacement:
                    allele_predicates["breakendReplacementString"] += 1
                if allele.breakend.is_single:
                    allele_predicates["isSingleBreakend"] += 1

        entries = parse_info_entries(info)
        for key, value in entries:
            if value is None:
                continue
            number = info_numbers.get(key, ".")
            if not (allele_uris and version.is_positional(key, number)):
                continue
            items = vocab.split_value_items(value)
            value_items += len(items)
            arity = version.tuple_arity(key)
            if arity is not None:
                tuple_items += len(items)
            for index in range(len(items)):
                link = version.value_item_link(key, number, index)
                if link.allele_index is not None and link.allele_index in allele_uris:
                    value_item_alleles += 1
                elif link.genotype_index is not None:
                    predicates["forGenotypeIndex"] += 1
                elif link.gt_allele_index is not None:
                    predicates["forGTAlleleIndex"] += 1
        if entries and alt_count:
            _count_sv_layer(
                classes, predicates, alleles=alleles, info_map=dict(entries),
                pos=row[1] if len(row) > 1 else "", version=version,
            )

        if samples:
            format_keys = (row[8].split(":") if len(row) > 8 and row[8] else [])
            payloads = row[9 : 9 + len(samples)]
            # A positional FORMAT cell is decomposed into vcfc:FieldValueItems
            # exactly as a positional INFO one is -- _emit_value_items is called
            # for both, from append_expanded_sample_rdf and from the INFO pass.
            # Counting only the INFO side made every file with a positional
            # FORMAT key (AD, ADALL, PL -- i.e. most real VCFs) fail validation
            # with the whole item layer reported as unexpected extra rows.
            #
            # The emitter requires at least one ALT before it decomposes, and
            # split_value_items returns nothing for a missing cell, so both
            # conditions are mirrored rather than re-derived.
            if alt_count and format_keys:
                for payload in payloads:
                    fields = payload.split(":") if payload else []
                    for key_index, key in enumerate(format_keys):
                        cell = fields[key_index] if key_index < len(fields) else ""
                        if not cell:
                            continue
                        number = format_numbers.get(key, ".")
                        if not version.is_positional(key, number):
                            continue
                        items = vocab.split_value_items(cell)
                        if not items:
                            continue
                        format_items += len(items)
                        if version.tuple_arity(key) is not None:
                            format_tuple_items += len(items)
                        for index in range(len(items)):
                            link = version.value_item_link(key, number, index)
                            if (
                                link.allele_index is not None
                                and link.allele_index in allele_uris
                            ):
                                format_item_alleles += 1
                            elif link.genotype_index is not None:
                                format_item_predicates["forGenotypeIndex"] += 1
                            elif link.gt_allele_index is not None:
                                format_item_predicates["forGTAlleleIndex"] += 1
            # A phase set is emitted per sample call from its non-empty PS/PSL/
            # PSO/PSQ cells, in the expanded profile only.
            phase_keys = [
                (index, key) for index, key in enumerate(format_keys)
                if key in vocab.PHASE_SET_FORMAT_KEYS
            ]
            if phase_keys:
                for payload in payloads:
                    fields = payload.split(":") if payload else []
                    _count_phase_set(phase_set_counts, {
                        key: fields[index] for index, key in phase_keys
                        if index < len(fields) and fields[index]
                    })
            if "GT" in format_keys:
                gt_index = format_keys.index("GT")
                for payload in payloads:
                    fields = payload.split(":") if payload else []
                    raw_gt = fields[gt_index] if gt_index < len(fields) else ""
                    parsed = vocab.parse_genotype(raw_gt)
                    if parsed is None:
                        continue
                    genotypes += 1
                    genotype_calls += len(parsed.calls)
                    called_alleles += sum(
                        1 for call in parsed.calls
                        if call.allele_index is not None and call.allele_index <= alt_count
                    )

    if reference_alleles:
        allele_classes["ReferenceAllele"] = reference_alleles
        allele_predicates["hasReferenceAllele"] = reference_alleles
    if alt_alleles:
        allele_classes["AltAllele"] = alt_alleles
        allele_predicates["hasAltAllele"] = alt_alleles
    total_alleles = reference_alleles + alt_alleles
    for name in ("alleleIndex", "alleleValue", "alleleKind"):
        allele_predicates[name] += total_alleles

    if value_items:
        classes["FieldValueItem"] += value_items
        for name in ("hasValueItem", "valueIndex", "itemValue"):
            predicates[name] += value_items
        predicates["forAllele"] += value_item_alleles
        predicates["tupleArity"] += tuple_items

    # The parsed genotype layer is expanded-only, so it is reported separately
    # and merged by expected_census for that profile alone. Keeping parse_vcf
    # representation-independent is what lets one parse serve both censuses.
    genotype_classes: Counter[str] = Counter()
    genotype_predicates: Counter[str] = Counter()
    if genotypes:
        genotype_classes["Genotype"] += genotypes
        genotype_classes["GenotypeAlleleCall"] += genotype_calls
        for name in ("hasGenotype", "genotypeString", "ploidy", "phasingStatus"):
            genotype_predicates[name] += genotypes
        for name in ("hasAlleleCall", "callIndex", "isNoCall"):
            genotype_predicates[name] += genotype_calls
        genotype_predicates["calledAllele"] += called_alleles
    # Phase sets travel with the expanded sample layer, as genotypes do.
    if phase_set_counts:
        genotype_classes["PhaseSet"] += phase_set_counts.pop("PhaseSet")
        genotype_predicates.update(phase_set_counts)

    format_item_classes: Counter[str] = Counter()
    if format_items:
        format_item_classes["FieldValueItem"] += format_items
        for name in ("hasValueItem", "valueIndex", "itemValue"):
            format_item_predicates[name] += format_items
        format_item_predicates["forAllele"] += format_item_alleles
        format_item_predicates["tupleArity"] += format_tuple_items

    return {
        "emittedRecordClasses": dict(classes),
        "emittedRecordPredicates": dict(predicates),
        "emittedAlleleClasses": dict(allele_classes),
        "emittedAllelePredicates": dict(allele_predicates),
        "emittedGenotypeClasses": dict(genotype_classes),
        "emittedGenotypePredicates": dict(genotype_predicates),
        "emittedFormatItemClasses": dict(format_item_classes),
        "emittedFormatItemPredicates": dict(format_item_predicates),
        "formatValueItemCount": format_items,
        "alleleCount": total_alleles,
        "valueItemCount": value_items,
        "genotypeCount": genotypes,
        "genotypeAlleleCallCount": genotype_calls,
    }

    samples: list[str],
    *,
    version: Any,
    contig_ids: set[str],
    alt_declaration_ids: set[str],
    has_assembly_line: bool = False,
    info_numbers: dict[str, str],
    format_numbers: dict[str, str],
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Counters for the allele, INFO, value-item, SV and genotype families.

    ``rows`` are the raw tab-split VCF data columns. Everything is derived from
    those and from the version, exactly as the emitters derive it.
    """
    classes: Counter[str] = Counter()
    predicates: Counter[str] = Counter()
    # The allele layer is reported separately for the same reason the genotype
    # layer is: it is not owned by one representation axis. Structured INFO
    # needs it for the Number=A/R/G value items, and the expanded sample layer
    # needs it for vcfc:calledAllele, so expected_census merges it when either
    # asks. Everything the emitter writes inside its ``emit_alleles`` branch --
    # the contig and assembly links as well as the allele resources -- belongs
    # here, or the oracle and the emitter would disagree about raw INFO.
    allele_classes: Counter[str] = Counter()
    allele_predicates: Counter[str] = Counter()

    assembly_contig_ids: set[str] = set()
    reference_alleles = alt_alleles = 0
    value_items = value_item_alleles = tuple_items = 0
    # FORMAT value items are counted separately: the emitter decomposes them
    # only in the expanded per-sample representation, so expected_census merges
    # them for that profile alone, exactly as it does the genotype layer.
    format_items = format_item_alleles = format_tuple_items = 0
    format_item_predicates: Counter[str] = Counter()
    genotypes = genotype_calls = called_alleles = 0

    for row in rows:
        chrom = row[0] if len(row) > 0 else ""
        ref = row[3] if len(row) > 3 else ""
        alt = row[4] if len(row) > 4 else ""
        info = row[7] if len(row) > 7 else ""

        # A bracketed CHROM names a breakpoint-assembly contig instead of a
        # declared reference sequence; the two are mutually exclusive.
        assembly_id = vocab.parse_bracketed_chrom(chrom)
        if assembly_id is not None:
            allele_predicates["chromAssemblyContig"] += 1
            if assembly_id not in assembly_contig_ids:
                assembly_contig_ids.add(assembly_id)
                allele_classes["AssemblyContig"] += 1
                allele_predicates["assemblyContigId"] += 1
                if has_assembly_line:
                    allele_predicates["declaredInAssembly"] += 1
        elif chrom in contig_ids:
            allele_predicates["chromosome"] += 1

        alleles = vocab.parse_alt_alleles(ref, alt)
        allele_uris = {allele.index for allele in alleles}
        alt_count = sum(1 for allele in alleles if allele.index >= 1)
        for allele in alleles:
            if allele.index == 0:
                reference_alleles += 1
            else:
                alt_alleles += 1
            if allele.symbolic_id and allele.symbolic_id in alt_declaration_ids:
                allele_predicates["declaredByAlt"] += 1
            if allele.symbolic_type:
                allele_predicates["svType"] += 1
            if allele.breakend is not None:
                allele_classes["Breakend"] += 1
                if allele.breakend.orientation is not None:
                    allele_predicates["breakendOrientation"] += 1
                if allele.breakend.replacement:
                    allele_predicates["breakendReplacementString"] += 1
                if allele.breakend.is_single:
                    allele_predicates["isSingleBreakend"] += 1

        entries = parse_info_entries(info)
        for key, value in entries:
            if value is None:
                continue
            number = info_numbers.get(key, ".")
            if not (allele_uris and version.is_positional(key, number)):
                continue
            items = vocab.split_value_items(value)
            value_items += len(items)
            arity = version.tuple_arity(key)
            if arity is not None:
                tuple_items += len(items)
            for index in range(len(items)):
                link = version.value_item_link(key, number, index)
                if link.allele_index is not None and link.allele_index in allele_uris:
                    value_item_alleles += 1
                elif link.genotype_index is not None:
                    predicates["forGenotypeIndex"] += 1
                elif link.gt_allele_index is not None:
                    predicates["forGTAlleleIndex"] += 1

        if samples:
            format_keys = (row[8].split(":") if len(row) > 8 and row[8] else [])
            payloads = row[9 : 9 + len(samples)]
            # A positional FORMAT cell is decomposed into vcfc:FieldValueItems
            # exactly as a positional INFO one is -- _emit_value_items is called
            # for both, from append_expanded_sample_rdf and from the INFO pass.
            # Counting only the INFO side made every file with a positional
            # FORMAT key (AD, ADALL, PL -- i.e. most real VCFs) fail validation
            # with the whole item layer reported as unexpected extra rows.
            #
            # The emitter requires at least one ALT before it decomposes, and
            # split_value_items returns nothing for a missing cell, so both
            # conditions are mirrored rather than re-derived.
            if alt_count and format_keys:
                for payload in payloads:
                    fields = payload.split(":") if payload else []
                    for key_index, key in enumerate(format_keys):
                        cell = fields[key_index] if key_index < len(fields) else ""
                        if not cell:
                            continue
                        number = format_numbers.get(key, ".")
                        if not version.is_positional(key, number):
                            continue
                        items = vocab.split_value_items(cell)
                        if not items:
                            continue
                        format_items += len(items)
                        if version.tuple_arity(key) is not None:
                            format_tuple_items += len(items)
                        for index in range(len(items)):
                            link = version.value_item_link(key, number, index)
                            if (
                                link.allele_index is not None
                                and link.allele_index in allele_uris
                            ):
                                format_item_alleles += 1
                            elif link.genotype_index is not None:
                                format_item_predicates["forGenotypeIndex"] += 1
                            elif link.gt_allele_index is not None:
                                format_item_predicates["forGTAlleleIndex"] += 1
            if "GT" in format_keys:
                gt_index = format_keys.index("GT")
                for payload in payloads:
                    fields = payload.split(":") if payload else []
                    raw_gt = fields[gt_index] if gt_index < len(fields) else ""
                    parsed = vocab.parse_genotype(raw_gt)
                    if parsed is None:
                        continue
                    genotypes += 1
                    genotype_calls += len(parsed.calls)
                    called_alleles += sum(
                        1 for call in parsed.calls
                        if call.allele_index is not None and call.allele_index <= alt_count
                    )

    if reference_alleles:
        allele_classes["ReferenceAllele"] = reference_alleles
        allele_predicates["hasReferenceAllele"] = reference_alleles
    if alt_alleles:
        allele_classes["AltAllele"] = alt_alleles
        allele_predicates["hasAltAllele"] = alt_alleles
    total_alleles = reference_alleles + alt_alleles
    for name in ("alleleIndex", "alleleValue", "alleleKind"):
        allele_predicates[name] += total_alleles

    if value_items:
        classes["FieldValueItem"] += value_items
        for name in ("hasValueItem", "valueIndex", "itemValue"):
            predicates[name] += value_items
        predicates["forAllele"] += value_item_alleles
        predicates["tupleArity"] += tuple_items

    # The parsed genotype layer is expanded-only, so it is reported separately
    # and merged by expected_census for that profile alone. Keeping parse_vcf
    # representation-independent is what lets one parse serve both censuses.
    genotype_classes: Counter[str] = Counter()
    genotype_predicates: Counter[str] = Counter()
    if genotypes:
        genotype_classes["Genotype"] += genotypes
        genotype_classes["GenotypeAlleleCall"] += genotype_calls
        for name in ("hasGenotype", "genotypeString", "ploidy", "phasingStatus"):
            genotype_predicates[name] += genotypes
        for name in ("hasAlleleCall", "callIndex", "isNoCall"):
            genotype_predicates[name] += genotype_calls
        genotype_predicates["calledAllele"] += called_alleles

    format_item_classes: Counter[str] = Counter()
    if format_items:
        format_item_classes["FieldValueItem"] += format_items
        for name in ("hasValueItem", "valueIndex", "itemValue"):
            format_item_predicates[name] += format_items
        format_item_predicates["forAllele"] += format_item_alleles
        format_item_predicates["tupleArity"] += format_tuple_items

    return {
        "emittedRecordClasses": dict(classes),
        "emittedRecordPredicates": dict(predicates),
        "emittedAlleleClasses": dict(allele_classes),
        "emittedAllelePredicates": dict(allele_predicates),
        "emittedGenotypeClasses": dict(genotype_classes),
        "emittedGenotypePredicates": dict(genotype_predicates),
        "emittedFormatItemClasses": dict(format_item_classes),
        "emittedFormatItemPredicates": dict(format_item_predicates),
        "formatValueItemCount": format_items,
        "alleleCount": total_alleles,
        "valueItemCount": value_items,
        "genotypeCount": genotypes,
        "genotypeAlleleCallCount": genotype_calls,
    }

items.summary: Lists every resource type (class) in the graph and how many resources have it, and checks that list against what the VCF implies.
items.notes: Counts distinct resources per asserted rdf:type, with no inference. This is why vcfc:FilterDefinition and vcfc:AltDefinition, which the vocabulary's subclass axioms imply for FILTER and ALT header lines, are not expected. Expectations are derived from the VCF and the emitters' documented shapes, never from the mapping rules, so a custom --rules mapping makes Q9-Q13 report-only (NOT_APPLICABLE_CUSTOM_MAPPING). The expected inventory depends on the sample profile (--representation expanded/condensed), --info-representation (structured/raw) and --header-representation (structured/basic). Header and data lines are read from the file text, not from cyvcf2's re-serialization. Tandem repeats, local alleles and base modifications are not counted yet, so a file using them fails Q9/Q10.
items.differences: The query is unchanged. v3.1.0's oracle does not count two layers that both versions' emitters write: phase sets (vcfc:PhaseSet, inPhaseSet, phaseSetId/Name/Ordinal/Quality, expanded profile) and the SV carriers (isImprecise/isNovel, svLength, svClaim, VariantEvent/eventType/inEvent, CIPOS/CIEND faldo:InRangePosition intervals, CILEN/CICN ConfidenceIntervals, gVCF ReferenceBlocks; structured INFO). Under v3.1.0 a VCF that carries them therefore fails Q9/Q10 even when the graph is right. This is the mismatch NG131FQA1I hit under v3.3.0, whose census oracle is identical to v3.1.0's. v3.3.1 counts them (commit 3994e94) and keys FALDO terms by their full IRI (_census_iri).

# Every asserted rdf:type and how many resources carry it. Complements the
# predicate census: together they bound both the properties and the resources

SELECT ?class (COUNT(DISTINCT ?resource) AS ?resourceCount)
WHERE {
  ?resource a ?class .
}
GROUP BY ?class
ORDER BY ?class

def emitted_record_counters(
    rows: list[list[str]],
    samples: list[str],
    *,
    version: Any,
    contig_ids: set[str],
    alt_declaration_ids: set[str],
    has_assembly_line: bool = False,
    info_numbers: dict[str, str],
    format_numbers: dict[str, str],
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Counters for the allele, INFO, value-item, SV and genotype families.

    ``rows`` are the raw tab-split VCF data columns. Everything is derived from
    those and from the version, exactly as the emitters derive it.
    """
    classes: Counter[str] = Counter()
    predicates: Counter[str] = Counter()
    # The allele layer is reported separately for the same reason the genotype
    # layer is: it is not owned by one representation axis. Structured INFO
    # needs it for the Number=A/R/G value items, and the expanded sample layer
    # needs it for vcfc:calledAllele, so expected_census merges it when either
    # asks. Everything the emitter writes inside its ``emit_alleles`` branch --
    # the contig and assembly links as well as the allele resources -- belongs
    # here, or the oracle and the emitter would disagree about raw INFO.
    allele_classes: Counter[str] = Counter()
    allele_predicates: Counter[str] = Counter()

    assembly_contig_ids: set[str] = set()
    reference_alleles = alt_alleles = 0
    value_items = value_item_alleles = tuple_items = 0
    # FORMAT value items are counted separately: the emitter decomposes them
    # only in the expanded per-sample representation, so expected_census merges
    # them for that profile alone, exactly as it does the genotype layer.
    format_items = format_item_alleles = format_tuple_items = 0
    format_item_predicates: Counter[str] = Counter()
    genotypes = genotype_calls = called_alleles = 0

    for row in rows:
        chrom = row[0] if len(row) > 0 else ""
        ref = row[3] if len(row) > 3 else ""
        alt = row[4] if len(row) > 4 else ""
        info = row[7] if len(row) > 7 else ""

        # A bracketed CHROM names a breakpoint-assembly contig instead of a
        # declared reference sequence; the two are mutually exclusive.
        assembly_id = vocab.parse_bracketed_chrom(chrom)
        if assembly_id is not None:
            allele_predicates["chromAssemblyContig"] += 1
            if assembly_id not in assembly_contig_ids:
                assembly_contig_ids.add(assembly_id)
                allele_classes["AssemblyContig"] += 1
                allele_predicates["assemblyContigId"] += 1
                if has_assembly_line:
                    allele_predicates["declaredInAssembly"] += 1
        elif chrom in contig_ids:
            allele_predicates["chromosome"] += 1

        alleles = vocab.parse_alt_alleles(ref, alt)
        allele_uris = {allele.index for allele in alleles}
        alt_count = sum(1 for allele in alleles if allele.index >= 1)
        for allele in alleles:
            if allele.index == 0:
                reference_alleles += 1
            else:
                alt_alleles += 1
            if allele.symbolic_id and allele.symbolic_id in alt_declaration_ids:
                allele_predicates["declaredByAlt"] += 1
            if allele.symbolic_type:
                allele_predicates["svType"] += 1
            if allele.breakend is not None:
                allele_classes["Breakend"] += 1
                if allele.breakend.orientation is not None:
                    allele_predicates["breakendOrientation"] += 1
                if allele.breakend.replacement:
                    allele_predicates["breakendReplacementString"] += 1
                if allele.breakend.is_single:
                    allele_predicates["isSingleBreakend"] += 1

        entries = parse_info_entries(info)
        for key, value in entries:
            if value is None:
                continue
            number = info_numbers.get(key, ".")
            if not (allele_uris and version.is_positional(key, number)):
                continue
            items = vocab.split_value_items(value)
            value_items += len(items)
            arity = version.tuple_arity(key)
            if arity is not None:
                tuple_items += len(items)
            for index in range(len(items)):
                link = version.value_item_link(key, number, index)
                if link.allele_index is not None and link.allele_index in allele_uris:
                    value_item_alleles += 1
                elif link.genotype_index is not None:
                    predicates["forGenotypeIndex"] += 1
                elif link.gt_allele_index is not None:
                    predicates["forGTAlleleIndex"] += 1

        if samples:
            format_keys = (row[8].split(":") if len(row) > 8 and row[8] else [])
            payloads = row[9 : 9 + len(samples)]
            # A positional FORMAT cell is decomposed into vcfc:FieldValueItems
            # exactly as a positional INFO one is -- _emit_value_items is called
            # for both, from append_expanded_sample_rdf and from the INFO pass.
            # Counting only the INFO side made every file with a positional
            # FORMAT key (AD, ADALL, PL -- i.e. most real VCFs) fail validation
            # with the whole item layer reported as unexpected extra rows.
            #
            # The emitter requires at least one ALT before it decomposes, and
            # split_value_items returns nothing for a missing cell, so both
            # conditions are mirrored rather than re-derived.
            if alt_count and format_keys:
                for payload in payloads:
                    fields = payload.split(":") if payload else []
                    for key_index, key in enumerate(format_keys):
                        cell = fields[key_index] if key_index < len(fields) else ""
                        if not cell:
                            continue
                        number = format_numbers.get(key, ".")
                        if not version.is_positional(key, number):
                            continue
                        items = vocab.split_value_items(cell)
                        if not items:
                            continue
                        format_items += len(items)
                        if version.tuple_arity(key) is not None:
                            format_tuple_items += len(items)
                        for index in range(len(items)):
                            link = version.value_item_link(key, number, index)
                            if (
                                link.allele_index is not None
                                and link.allele_index in allele_uris
                            ):
                                format_item_alleles += 1
                            elif link.genotype_index is not None:
                                format_item_predicates["forGenotypeIndex"] += 1
                            elif link.gt_allele_index is not None:
                                format_item_predicates["forGTAlleleIndex"] += 1
            if "GT" in format_keys:
                gt_index = format_keys.index("GT")
                for payload in payloads:
                    fields = payload.split(":") if payload else []
                    raw_gt = fields[gt_index] if gt_index < len(fields) else ""
                    parsed = vocab.parse_genotype(raw_gt)
                    if parsed is None:
                        continue
                    genotypes += 1
                    genotype_calls += len(parsed.calls)
                    called_alleles += sum(
                        1 for call in parsed.calls
                        if call.allele_index is not None and call.allele_index <= alt_count
                    )

    if reference_alleles:
        allele_classes["ReferenceAllele"] = reference_alleles
        allele_predicates["hasReferenceAllele"] = reference_alleles
    if alt_alleles:
        allele_classes["AltAllele"] = alt_alleles
        allele_predicates["hasAltAllele"] = alt_alleles
    total_alleles = reference_alleles + alt_alleles
    for name in ("alleleIndex", "alleleValue", "alleleKind"):
        allele_predicates[name] += total_alleles

    if value_items:
        classes["FieldValueItem"] += value_items
        for name in ("hasValueItem", "valueIndex", "itemValue"):
            predicates[name] += value_items
        predicates["forAllele"] += value_item_alleles
        predicates["tupleArity"] += tuple_items

    # The parsed genotype layer is expanded-only, so it is reported separately
    # and merged by expected_census for that profile alone. Keeping parse_vcf
    # representation-independent is what lets one parse serve both censuses.
    genotype_classes: Counter[str] = Counter()
    genotype_predicates: Counter[str] = Counter()
    if genotypes:
        genotype_classes["Genotype"] += genotypes
        genotype_classes["GenotypeAlleleCall"] += genotype_calls
        for name in ("hasGenotype", "genotypeString", "ploidy", "phasingStatus"):
            genotype_predicates[name] += genotypes
        for name in ("hasAlleleCall", "callIndex", "isNoCall"):
            genotype_predicates[name] += genotype_calls
        genotype_predicates["calledAllele"] += called_alleles

    format_item_classes: Counter[str] = Counter()
    if format_items:
        format_item_classes["FieldValueItem"] += format_items
        for name in ("hasValueItem", "valueIndex", "itemValue"):
            format_item_predicates[name] += format_items
        format_item_predicates["forAllele"] += format_item_alleles
        format_item_predicates["tupleArity"] += format_tuple_items

    return {
        "emittedRecordClasses": dict(classes),
        "emittedRecordPredicates": dict(predicates),
        "emittedAlleleClasses": dict(allele_classes),
        "emittedAllelePredicates": dict(allele_predicates),
        "emittedGenotypeClasses": dict(genotype_classes),
        "emittedGenotypePredicates": dict(genotype_predicates),
        "emittedFormatItemClasses": dict(format_item_classes),
        "emittedFormatItemPredicates": dict(format_item_predicates),
        "formatValueItemCount": format_items,
        "alleleCount": total_alleles,
        "valueItemCount": value_items,
        "genotypeCount": genotypes,
        "genotypeAlleleCallCount": genotype_calls,
    }

items.summary: Fingerprints every record (position, alleles, QUAL, FILTER and INFO, bound to the record's own IRI) into 256 hash buckets and checks that the bucket counts match the VCF, so values swapped between records are caught.

for n, columns in enumerate(raw tab-split data lines of the file, start=1):   # kept aligned with cyvcf2
    record_iri = f"file://{source_component}#record/{n}"
    qual = columns[5]
    if re.search(r"\.[0-9]*0$", qual):                        # digest_qual(), v3.3.1 only
        qual = re.sub(r"\.?0+$", "", qual)                    # "30.10" -> "30.1", "30.0" -> "30"; "100", "." unchanged
    fields = [record_iri, *columns[0:5], qual, *columns[6:8]]  # IRI, CHROM, POS, ID, REF, ALT, QUAL, FILTER, INFO

items.notes: Hashes the raw lexical columns read from the file text (not cyvcf2's typed accessors) and binds them to the record IRI, so values permuted between records change the histogram. The record IRI is built from the VCF file name and the 1-based record index, so the check assumes the shipped mapping's IRI templates (report-only under a custom mapping). PREFIX vcfc: <https://w3id.org/vcf-core/vocab#>

# Per-record identity, aggregated into a fixed-size histogram.
#
# Every other core query is a GROUP BY count, so values permuted between
# records are invisible to all of them: swap POS between two records in the
# same 1 Mb window and nothing changes. This closes that gap.
#
# The record IRI is hashed together with its values. That binding is the whole
# point: digesting the values alone would give a permutation the same multiset
# and change nothing. Bucketing on the first byte of the hash keeps the result
# at most 256 rows for any graph size, and a mismatch is localized by
# re-querying only the differing buckets.
#
# Fields are separated by U+001F (unit separator), written as a SPARQL UCHAR
# escape. It cannot appear in a VCF field, so no combination of values can be
# made to collide by shifting a field boundary.
SELECT ?bucket (COUNT(*) AS ?recordCount)
WHERE {
  ?record a vcfc:VCFRecord ;
          vcfc:chrom ?chrom ;
          vcfc:pos ?pos ;
          vcfc:recordId ?recordIdLiteral ;
          vcfc:ref ?ref ;
          vcfc:alt ?alt ;
          vcfc:hasCall ?call .
  ?call vcfc:qual ?qual ;
        vcfc:filter ?filter ;
        vcfc:infoRaw ?info .
  BIND(SUBSTR(SHA256(CONCAT(
    STR(?record),          "\u001F",
    STR(?chrom),           "\u001F",
    STR(?pos),             "\u001F",
    STR(?recordIdLiteral), "\u001F",
    STR(?ref),             "\u001F",
    STR(?alt),             "\u001F",
    STR(?qual),            "\u001F",
    STR(?filter),          "\u001F",
    STR(?info)
  )), 1, 2) AS ?bucket)
}
GROUP BY ?bucket
ORDER BY ?bucket

#
# Fields are separated by U+001F (unit separator), written as a SPARQL UCHAR
# escape. It cannot appear in a VCF field, so no combination of values can be
# made to collide by shifting a field boundary.
#
# QUAL is an xsd:decimal, and engines disagree on how STR() spells one: QLever
# returns the canonical value ("30.1"), others the lexical form ("30.10"). So
# trailing zeros after the decimal point are dropped here, and the oracle drops
# them the same way (digest_qual), making the digest compare values rather than
# spellings. Nothing else changes: "100" stays "100" and "." stays ".".
SELECT ?bucket (COUNT(*) AS ?recordCount)
WHERE {

          vcfc:chrom ?chrom ;
          vcfc:pos ?pos ;
          vcfc:recordId ?recordIdLiteral ;
          vcfc:ref ?ref ;
          vcfc:alt ?alt ;
          vcfc:hasCall ?call .
  ?call vcfc:qual ?qual ;
        vcfc:filter ?filter ;
        vcfc:infoRaw ?info .
  BIND(STR(?qual) AS ?qualText)
  BIND(IF(REGEX(?qualText, "\\.[0-9]*0$"), REPLACE(?qualText, "\\.?0+$", ""), ?qualText)
       AS ?qualKey)
  BIND(SUBSTR(SHA256(CONCAT(
    STR(?record),          "\u001F",
    STR(?chrom),           "\u001F",
    STR(?pos),             "\u001F",
    STR(?recordIdLiteral), "\u001F",
    STR(?ref),             "\u001F",
    STR(?alt),             "\u001F",
    ?qualKey,              "\u001F",
    STR(?filter),          "\u001F",
    STR(?info)

def parse_info_entries(info: str) -> list[tuple[str, str | None]]:
    """Split an INFO column into ``(key, value)`` pairs.

    An entry without ``=`` is a Flag: a presence assertion with no value, which
    the vocabulary models as ``vcfc:fieldValueBoolean true``.
    """
    if info in ("", "."):
        return []
    entries: list[tuple[str, str | None]] = []
    for item in info.split(";"):
        if not item:
            continue
        key, separator, value = item.partition("=")
        entries.append((key, value if separator else None))
    return entries

def sample_uri_ids(sample_ids: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """Derive each sample's IRI component the way the emitters do.

    Mirrors ``_sample_id_to_uri_id`` in ``vcf_rdfizer.py``, including the
    occurrence suffix that keeps two samples whose ids sanitize to the same
    string distinguishable.
    """
    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    out: list[str] = []
    for index, sample_id in enumerate(sample_ids, start=1):
        base = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._~-]+", "_", sample_id).strip("_") or f"sample_{index}"
        counts[base] = counts.get(base, 0) + 1
        out.append(f"{base}_{counts[base]}" if counts[base] > 1 else base)
    return out

# xsd:decimal, xsd:double, a plain literal - is still reported.

WHERE {
  ?record a vcfc:VCFRecord ; vcfc:pos ?pos .
  FILTER(DATATYPE(?pos) NOT IN (
    xsd:integer, xsd:int, xsd:long, xsd:short, xsd:byte,
    xsd:nonNegativeInteger, xsd:positiveInteger,
    xsd:unsignedLong, xsd:unsignedInt, xsd:unsignedShort, xsd:unsignedByte
  ))
}

      IF(STR(?s) = "" || STR(?p) = "" || (ISIRI(?o) && STR(?o) = ""), "EMPTY_IRI", "")

  )
  FILTER(?issue != "")
}

items.label: Carriers query
items.summary: Lists, for each participant, the variants they carry that ClinVar has classified (with at least one review star) in one of the 81 ACMG secondary-findings genes, joining participant VCFs and ClinVar through a shared variant identifier.
items.pseudo:
# Conventional workflow (baseline.sh + baseline_carriers.py): bcftools and a hand-written consent script, no RDF
for id in participants:
    if first CHROM of id.acmg.vcf.gz starts with "chr": bcftools annotate --rename-chrs chrN->N
    bcftools annotate -a clinvar.acmg.vcf.gz -c INFO/CLNSIG,INFO/CLNREVSTAT,INFO/GENEINFO --pair-logic exact \
      | bcftools view -f PASS,. -i 'INFO/CLNSIG!="." && GT="alt"' \
      | bcftools query -i 'GT="alt"' -f "id CHROM POS REF ALT CLNSIG CLNREVSTAT GENEINFO [GT]" >> genotypes.tsv
for (participant, chrom, pos, ref, alt, clnsig, revstat, geneinfo, gt) in genotypes.tsv:
    if revstat in excluded_review_status: continue          # no_assertion_criteria_provided, no_classification_*
    for gene in sorted({item.split(":")[0] for item in geneinfo.split("|")} & ACMG_GENES):
        carrier(participant, gene, chrom without 'chr', pos, ref, alt, classification=clnsig.split("|")[0], gt,
                restricted=REF extent overlaps a cancer-predisposition gene span)
for requester in requesters:   # plus 'unrestricted' = every carrier
    carriers.<requester>.tsv = [c for c in carriers if released(c, purpose, policy, assignee, panels)]
# compare.py: key sets (participant, gene, chrom, pos, ref, alt) must be equal for every requester
items.notes: The four scenario copies are byte-identical (SHA-256 abcb5f4f..., checked at testing HEAD 47f1e942); all are written by generate.py (carriers_query, generate.py 219-278; written at 311-315) from the case file and acmg_sf_v3.2.genes.txt, so 'per scenario' differences live in the policy and the inputs, not in the query. Relative to harness commit e3743590 the queries changed only in a comment (lines 11-12). The query joins participant calls and ClinVar on the SPDI IRI written by the spdi linker (vcfl:sameVariantAs), keeps calls with vcfc:filterStatus FiltersPassed or FiltersNotApplied and a genotype string containing a non-zero allele (REGEX "[1-9]"), excludes the three unstarred review statuses, and matches a GENEINFO symbol against the 81 ACMG genes. Consent is not in the query: it is applied by vcf-rdfizer-policy views, and the query runs once over each requester's view plus ClinVar and its links, and once over everything as 'unrestricted' (17_use_case_acmg.sh 422-458; run_query.py loads each input as its own named graph into QLever and clears the cache before each replicate). On the baseline side consent is the hand-written released() function; the cancer-gene restriction is decided by REF-extent overlap with gene spans (regions.json), the RDF side by vcfl:overlapsGene links. Agreement check (compare.py): for 'unrestricted' and every requester whose query ran, the baseline's carriers.<requester>.tsv and the RDF route's query/<requester>/carriers.tsv are reduced to sets of keys (participant, gene, CHROM without 'chr', POS, REF, ALT), with the participant taken from ?file (file://<participant>.acmg.vcf); the two sets must be equal. Classification, CLNSIG and GT are not part of the key. Where both routes wrote rare.tsv the rare lists are compared the same way, and where governed views exist each view's released record count must equal the baseline's per-requester count over every record (records.tsv). compare.py exits 1 unless at least one requester ran and every comparison agrees. Reported v3.3.1 reruns: carrier lists agree for every requester in all four scenarios (Scenario 1 unrestricted 7,211; Scenario 2 173,102; Scenario 3 1,496; Scenario 4 1,382). Scenario 2's record-level view check disagrees (cardio 685,928 vs 685,818; biobank 356,835 vs 356,777): per benchmark-results/vcf-bench-1/v331-rerun/README.md every differing record is a symbolic structural variant in a cancer-predisposition gene that v3.3.1's gene linkers do not link, a limitation the paper states.

# GENERATED by generate.py from use_case.json; do not edit.
#
# Carriers of a ClinVar-classified variant in an ACMG SF v3.2 gene, with the
# classification returned rather than filtered on. Run it over a requester's
# release view plus the ClinVar graph and the link graphs; what the view
# withholds cannot match.
#
# Two tables joined on the SPDI identifier both sides link to, never on the
# files' own IRIs or contig names. Each table is a subquery so an engine plans
# it on its own: as one group of ~20 patterns, QLever's planner either takes
# exponential time or picks a cross product (observed on the
# first arm 1 run, 2026-09-28).

PREFIX vcfc: <https://w3id.org/vcf-core/vocab#>
PREFIX vcfl: <https://w3id.org/vcf-rdfizer/linking#>

SELECT DISTINCT ?file ?sample ?gene ?chrom ?pos ?ref ?alt ?variant ?clnsig ?gt
WHERE {
  # Genome calls that carry the ALT, FILTER PASS or missing.
  { SELECT ?file ?sample ?chrom ?pos ?ref ?alt ?variant ?gt WHERE {
      ?file vcfc:hasRecord ?record .
      ?record vcfc:chrom ?chrom ; vcfc:pos ?pos ; vcfc:ref ?ref ; vcfc:alt ?alt ;
              vcfc:hasCall ?call .
      ?call vcfc:filterStatus ?status ; vcfc:hasSampleCall ?sampleCall ;
            vcfl:sameVariantAs ?variant .
      ?sampleCall vcfc:sampleId ?sample ; vcfc:hasGenotype ?genotype .
      ?genotype vcfc:genotypeString ?gt .
      FILTER(?status IN (vcfc:FiltersPassed, vcfc:FiltersNotApplied))
      FILTER(STRSTARTS(STR(?variant), "https://api.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/variation/v0/spdi/"))
      FILTER(REGEX(STR(?gt), "[1-9]"))
      FILTER(?file != <file://clinvar.acmg.vcf>) } }

  # ClinVar's classification and gene annotation for each variant, one star or more.
  { SELECT ?variant ?clnsig ?geneinfo WHERE {
      <file://clinvar.acmg.vcf> vcfc:hasRecord ?cvRecord .
      ?cvRecord vcfc:hasCall ?clinvar .
      ?clinvar vcfl:sameVariantAs ?variant ;
               vcfc:hasInfoValue ?sig , ?rev , ?info .
      ?sig vcfc:declaredBy ?sigDef ; vcfc:fieldValue ?clnsig .
      ?sigDef vcfc:fieldId "CLNSIG" .
      ?rev vcfc:declaredBy ?revDef ; vcfc:fieldValue ?revstat .
      ?revDef vcfc:fieldId "CLNREVSTAT" .
      ?info vcfc:declaredBy ?infoDef ; vcfc:fieldValue ?geneinfo .
      ?infoDef vcfc:fieldId "GENEINFO" .
      FILTER(STR(?revstat) NOT IN ("no_assertion_criteria_provided", "no_classification_provided", "no_classification_for_the_individual_variant")) } }

  # The ACMG genes ClinVar names, matched after the join so the gene list meets

# files' own IRIs or contig names. Each table is a subquery so an engine plans
# it on its own: as one group of ~20 patterns, QLever's planner either takes
# exponential time or picks a cross product (observed on the
# first arm 1 run, 2026-09-28).

PREFIX vcfc: <https://w3id.org/vcf-core/vocab#>
PREFIX vcfl: <https://w3id.org/vcf-rdfizer/linking#>

SELECT DISTINCT ?file ?sample ?gene ?chrom ?pos ?ref ?alt ?variant ?clnsig ?gt ?af
WHERE {
  # Genome calls that carry the ALT, FILTER PASS or missing.
  { SELECT ?file ?sample ?chrom ?pos ?ref ?alt ?variant ?gt WHERE {
      ?file vcfc:hasRecord ?record .
      ?record vcfc:chrom ?chrom ; vcfc:pos ?pos ; vcfc:ref ?ref ; vcfc:alt ?alt ;
              vcfc:hasCall ?call .
      ?call vcfc:filterStatus ?status ; vcfc:hasSampleCall ?sampleCall ;
            vcfl:sameVariantAs ?variant .
      ?sampleCall vcfc:sampleId ?sample ; vcfc:hasGenotype ?genotype .
      ?genotype vcfc:genotypeString ?gt .
      FILTER(?status IN (vcfc:FiltersPassed, vcfc:FiltersNotApplied))
      FILTER(STRSTARTS(STR(?variant), "https://api.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/variation/v0/spdi/"))
      FILTER(REGEX(STR(?gt), "[1-9]"))
      FILTER(?file != <file://clinvar.acmg.vcf>) } }

  # ClinVar's classification and gene annotation for each variant, one star or more.
  { SELECT ?variant ?clnsig ?geneinfo WHERE {
      <file://clinvar.acmg.vcf> vcfc:hasRecord ?cvRecord .
      ?cvRecord vcfc:hasCall ?clinvar .
      ?clinvar vcfl:sameVariantAs ?variant ;
               vcfc:hasInfoValue ?sig , ?rev , ?info .
      ?sig vcfc:declaredBy ?sigDef ; vcfc:fieldValue ?clnsig .
      ?sigDef vcfc:fieldId "CLNSIG" .
      ?rev vcfc:declaredBy ?revDef ; vcfc:fieldValue ?revstat .
      ?revDef vcfc:fieldId "CLNREVSTAT" .
      ?info vcfc:declaredBy ?infoDef ; vcfc:fieldValue ?geneinfo .
      ?infoDef vcfc:fieldId "GENEINFO" .
      FILTER(STR(?revstat) NOT IN ("no_assertion_criteria_provided", "no_classification_provided", "no_classification_for_the_individual_variant")) } }

  # The panel's frequency for each variant, recorded once in its own sites-only
  # file rather than in every participant's.
  { SELECT ?variant ?af WHERE {
      <file://panel.acmg.vcf> vcfc:hasRecord ?panelRecord .
      ?panelRecord vcfc:hasCall ?panelCall .
      ?panelCall vcfl:sameVariantAs ?variant ; vcfc:hasInfoValue ?frequency .
      ?frequency vcfc:declaredBy ?frequencyDef ; vcfc:fieldValueDecimal ?af .
      ?frequencyDef vcfc:fieldId "AF" .
      FILTER(?af < 0.01) } }

  # The ACMG genes ClinVar names, matched after the join so the gene list meets
  # only the joined rows, not every ClinVar record.
  VALUES ?gene { "ACTA2" "ACTC1" "ACVRL1" "APC" "APOB" "ATP7B" "BAG3" "BMPR1A" "BRCA1" "BRCA2" "BTD" "CACNA1S" "CALM1" "CALM2" "CALM3" "CASQ2" "COL3A1" "DES" "DSC2" "DSG2" "DSP" "ENG" "FBN1" "FLNC" "GAA" "GLA" "HFE" "HNF1A" "KCNH2" "KCNQ1" "LDLR" "LMNA" "MAX" "MEN1" "MLH1" "MSH2" "MSH6" "MUTYH" "MYBPC3" "MYH11" "MYH7" "MYL2" "MYL3" "NF2" "OTC" "PALB2" "PCSK9" "PKP2" "PMS2" "PRKAG2" "PTEN" "RB1" "RBM20" "RET" "RPE65" "RYR1" "RYR2" "SCN5A" "SDHAF2" "SDHB" "SDHC" "SDHD" "SMAD3" "SMAD4" "STK11" "TGFBR1" "TGFBR2" "TMEM127" "TMEM43" "TNNC1" "TNNI3" "TNNT2" "TP53" "TPM1" "TRDN" "TSC1" "TSC2" "TTN" "TTR" "VHL" "WT1" }
  FILTER(REGEX(STR(?geneinfo), CONCAT("(^|\\|)", ?gene, ":")))
}
ORDER BY ?file ?gene ?pos ?alt

groups.title: Converter comparison: Q1–Q8 in each converter's vocabulary
groups.intro: Each content question is ported to each converter's vocabulary and run on QLever. The oracle is the validator's own, imported from the VCF-RDFizer image, so every converter is held to the same expected answers.

items.label: Q1 · Record density per 1 Mb window (converter comparison)
items.summary: Counts how many variant records fall in each 1-megabase window of each chromosome.
items.pseudo:
# oracle = validation_runner.parse_vcf(source_vcf, filter_oracle="auto"): one cyvcf2 pass
for v in VCF(source_vcf, strict_gt=True):
    density[(str(v.CHROM), (int(v.POS) - 1) // 1_000_000)] += 1
q01 = [{"chrom": c, "windowIndex": w, "recordCount": n} for (c, w), n in sorted(density.items())]
# per converter: normalize(SPARQL JSON) then compare_rows keyed on (chrom, windowIndex), value recordCount
items.notes: compare_converters.py runs inside the pinned VCF-RDFizer 3.3.1 image and imports that image's validator unchanged, so every converter's graph is held to the validator's own Q1-Q8 oracle (validation_runner.parse_vcf: one cyvcf2 pass, plus bcftools for FILTER when available), the same QLever engine, the same normalisation and the same comparator; only the SPARQL differs. Each question needs exactly one of a ported query or a not_represented.json reason, or the script refuses to run (compare_converters.py 120-134). VCF-RDFizer's own queries in the testing repo are verbatim copies of the v3.3.1 validator queries (SHA-256 identical, re-checked here; 18_converter_comparison.sh 140-146 checks them against the image). Inputs: HG005_GRCh38_r100000 (100,000 records x 1 sample) and 1000G_10000r_s16 (10,000 x 16). The reported run (benchmark-results/vcf-bench-1/18_converter_comparison/, harness e3743590) used the same query files and compare_converters.py as testing HEAD 47f1e942 (no diff in benchmarks/converters/queries or compare_converters.py). Ports: JVarkit reads CHROM from its urn:chrom/ IRI and counts <urn:variant/CHROM:POS:REF> records; TogoVar regroups allele nodes on (reference, POS, REF, ID) and maps its reference IRI back to CHROM through {{CHROM_VALUES}}, filled per input from TogoVar's own generated config (18_converter_comparison.sh 162-171, 296-297); SPARQLing Genomics regroups calls on floor(k / samples) from its origin://<md5>@<k> call IRIs, so only records with at least one non-reference call exist; BioInterchange uses g:locus landmark and start. sparql.label: Q1 · Record density per 1 Mb window (JVarkit port)
sparql.text:
PREFIX vcf: <http://github.com/lindenb/jvarkit/>
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
# JVarkit vcf2rdf (commit fc2356a3), run with --hide '' so ALT, FILTER and GT are written.
# Its classes are written as IRIs with the scheme "vcf" (<vcf:Variant>), not as prefixed names,
# so they are matched literally. A record is <urn:variant/CHROM:POS:REF>.
SELECT ?chrom ?windowIndex (COUNT(DISTINCT ?record) AS ?recordCount)
WHERE {
  ?record a <vcf:Variant> ; vcf:chrom ?chromIri ; vcf:position ?pos .
  BIND(STRAFTER(STR(?chromIri), "urn:chrom/") AS ?chrom)
  BIND(xsd:integer(FLOOR((xsd:integer(?pos) - 1) / 1000000)) AS ?windowIndex)
}
GROUP BY ?chrom ?windowIndex
ORDER BY ?chrom ?windowIndex

sparql.label: Q1 · Record density per 1 Mb window (TogoVar port)
sparql.text:
PREFIX gvo: <http://genome-variation.org/resource#>
PREFIX faldo: <http://biohackathon.org/resource/faldo#>
PREFIX dct: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/>
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
# TogoVar vcf2rdf v1.0.0-beta.12, run with --no-normalize so gvo:pos/ref/alt keep the VCF values.
# It writes one node per ALT allele and no node for the record, so records are regrouped on
# (reference, POS, REF, ID), all of which every allele node carries.
# CHROM is not written: TogoVar replaces it with the reference IRI its configuration assigns.
# {{CHROM_VALUES}} maps each IRI back to the CHROM it was assigned from, using the configuration
# file of this conversion (written by `vcf2rdf generate config`).
SELECT ?chrom ?windowIndex (COUNT(DISTINCT ?record) AS ?recordCount)
WHERE {
    ?allele gvo:pos ?pos ; gvo:ref ?refLiteral ; dct:identifier ?id ;
            faldo:location/(faldo:reference|faldo:begin/faldo:reference) ?seq .
    BIND(CONCAT(STR(?seq), "|", STR(?pos), "|", STR(?refLiteral), "|", STR(?id)) AS ?record)
  {{CHROM_VALUES}}
  BIND(xsd:integer(FLOOR((xsd:integer(?pos) - 1) / 1000000)) AS ?windowIndex)
}
GROUP BY ?chrom ?windowIndex
ORDER BY ?chrom ?windowIndex

sparql.label: Q1 · Record density per 1 Mb window (SPARQLing Genomics port)
sparql.text:
PREFIX sg: <https://sparqling-genomics.org/0.99.11/>
PREFIX vc: <sg://0.99.11/vcf2rdf/>
PREFIX v: <sg://0.99.11/vcf2rdf/variant/>
PREFIX gt: <sg://0.99.11/vcf2rdf/format/GT/>
PREFIX hdr: <sg://0.99.11/vcf2rdf/header/>
PREFIX faldo: <http://biohackathon.org/resource/faldo#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
# SPARQLing Genomics vcf2rdf 0.99.11, default options. It writes one vc:VariantCall per record and
# sample, and only for calls with a non-reference allele; there is no record node. Call IRIs are
# origin://<md5>@<k> with k = record index x samples + sample index (doc/command-line-tools.tex),
# so records are regrouped on floor(k / samples). Only the first ALT allele is written.
SELECT ?chrom ?windowIndex (COUNT(?record) AS ?recordCount)
WHERE {
  {
    SELECT ?record (SAMPLE(?chromIri) AS ?chromValue) (SAMPLE(?position) AS ?pos)
    WHERE {
    { SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?sampleNode) AS ?samples) WHERE { ?sampleNode a sg:Sample } }
      ?call a vc:VariantCall ; faldo:reference ?chromIri ; faldo:position ?position .
    BIND(xsd:integer(FLOOR(xsd:integer(STRAFTER(STR(?call), "@")) / ?samples)) AS ?record)
    }
    GROUP BY ?record
  }
  BIND(STRAFTER(STR(?chromValue), "http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/") AS ?chrom)
  BIND(xsd:integer(FLOOR((xsd:integer(?pos) - 1) / 1000000)) AS ?windowIndex)
}
GROUP BY ?chrom ?windowIndex
ORDER BY ?chrom ?windowIndex

sparql.label: Q1 · Record density per 1 Mb window (BioInterchange port)
sparql.text:
PREFIX g: <https://www.codamono.com/gfvo-squared#>
PREFIX gu: <https://www.codamono.com/gfvo-squared#unknownProperty->
PREFIX gc: <https://github.com/BioInterchange/Ontologies/gfvo-squared#>
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
# BioInterchange 2.0.5: GFVO-squared JSON-LD, one gc:Feature (a blank node) per record, with the
# header on a gc:Meta node. ALT alleles are g:alleleB, g:alleleC, ... in file order; "*" is
# written as "".
SELECT ?chrom ?windowIndex (COUNT(DISTINCT ?record) AS ?recordCount)
WHERE {
  ?record a gc:Feature ; g:locus ?locus .
  ?locus g:landmark ?landmark ; g:start ?pos .
  BIND(STR(?landmark) AS ?chrom)
  BIND(xsd:integer(FLOOR((xsd:integer(?pos) - 1) / 1000000)) AS ?windowIndex)
}
GROUP BY ?chrom ?windowIndex
ORDER BY ?chrom ?windowIndex

items.label: Q2 · Variant shape counts (converter comparison)
items.summary: Sorts every record into an allele-shape class (SNV, insertion, deletion, multiallelic, symbolic, ...) and counts each class.
items.notes: compare_converters.py runs inside the pinned VCF-RDFizer 3.3.1 image and imports that image's validator unchanged, so every converter's graph is held to the validator's own Q1-Q8 oracle (validation_runner.parse_vcf: one cyvcf2 pass, plus bcftools for FILTER when available), the same QLever engine, the same normalisation and the same comparator; only the SPARQL differs. Each question needs exactly one of a ported query or a not_represented.json reason, or the script refuses to run (compare_converters.py 120-134). VCF-RDFizer's own queries in the testing repo are verbatim copies of the v3.3.1 validator queries (SHA-256 identical, re-checked here; 18_converter_comparison.sh 140-146 checks them against the image). Inputs: HG005_GRCh38_r100000 (100,000 records x 1 sample) and 1000G_10000r_s16 (10,000 x 16). The reported run (benchmark-results/vcf-bench-1/18_converter_comparison/, harness e3743590) used the same query files and compare_converters.py as testing HEAD 47f1e942 (no diff in benchmarks/converters/queries or compare_converters.py). Port conflations from the README and the query comments: JVarkit writes one vcf:alt per allele with symbolic alleles and breakends as "" (the port maps "" to SYMBOLIC_OR_BREAKEND and counts distinct ALTs for MULTIALLELIC); TogoVar drops alleles outside [ACGTURYKMSWBDHVN] (symbolic, *, breakends); SPARQLing Genomics writes only the first ALT, so a record is read as MULTIALLELIC only when a written call carries an allele index >= 2; BioInterchange writes "*" as "" and the port restores it. Reported outcomes (HG005 / 1000G): VCF-RDFizer pass/pass, JVarkit pass/differs, TogoVar differs/differs, SPARQLing Genomics pass/differs, BioInterchange pass/pass.

sparql.label: Q2 · Variant shape counts (VCF-RDFizer, validator query)
sparql.text:
PREFIX vcfc: <https://w3id.org/vcf-core/vocab#>

SELECT ?variantClass (COUNT(DISTINCT ?record) AS ?recordCount)
WHERE {
  ?record a vcfc:VCFRecord ; vcfc:ref ?refLiteral ; vcfc:alt ?altLiteral .
  BIND(UCASE(STR(?refLiteral)) AS ?ref)
  BIND(UCASE(STR(?altLiteral)) AS ?alt)
  BIND(
    IF(?alt = ".", "NO_ALT",
      IF(CONTAINS(?alt, ","), "MULTIALLELIC",
        IF(
          ?alt = "*" || CONTAINS(?alt, "[") || CONTAINS(?alt, "]") ||
          (STRSTARTS(?alt, "<") && STRENDS(?alt, ">")),
          "SYMBOLIC_OR_BREAKEND",
          IF(
            !REGEX(?ref, "^[ACGTN]+$") || !REGEX(?alt, "^[ACGTN]+$"),
            "OTHER",
            IF(
              STRLEN(?ref) = 1 && STRLEN(?alt) = 1,
              "SNV",
              IF(
                STRLEN(?ref) = STRLEN(?alt),
                "MNV_OR_EQUAL_LENGTH_SUBSTITUTION",
                IF(STRLEN(?ref) < STRLEN(?alt), "INSERTION_SHAPE", "DELETION_SHAPE")
              )
            )
          )
        )
      )
    ) AS ?variantClass
  )
}
GROUP BY ?variantClass
ORDER BY ?variantClass

sparql.label: Q2 · Variant shape counts (JVarkit port)
sparql.text:
PREFIX vcf: <http://github.com/lindenb/jvarkit/>
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
# JVarkit vcf2rdf (commit fc2356a3), run with --hide '' so ALT, FILTER and GT are written.
# Its classes are written as IRIs with the scheme "vcf" (<vcf:Variant>), not as prefixed names,
# so they are matched literally. A record is <urn:variant/CHROM:POS:REF>.
# One vcf:alt literal per ALT allele, REF excluded; a symbolic allele or breakend is written as "".
SELECT ?variantClass (COUNT(?record) AS ?recordCount)
WHERE {
  {
    SELECT ?record (SAMPLE(?refLiteral) AS ?refValue) (SAMPLE(?altLiteral) AS ?altValue)
           (COUNT(DISTINCT ?altLiteral) AS ?nAlt)
    WHERE {
      ?record a <vcf:Variant> ; vcf:ref ?refLiteral .
      OPTIONAL { ?record vcf:alt ?altLiteral }
    }
    GROUP BY ?record
  }
  BIND(UCASE(STR(?refValue)) AS ?ref)
  BIND(UCASE(COALESCE(STR(?altValue), "")) AS ?alt)
  BIND(IF(?nAlt = 0, "NO_ALT", IF(?nAlt > 1, "MULTIALLELIC",
    IF(?alt = "" || ?alt = "*" || CONTAINS(?alt, "[") || CONTAINS(?alt, "]") ||
       (STRSTARTS(?alt, "<") && STRENDS(?alt, ">")), "SYMBOLIC_OR_BREAKEND",
    IF(!REGEX(?ref, "^[ACGTN]+$") || !REGEX(?alt, "^[ACGTN]+$"), "OTHER",
    IF(STRLEN(?ref) = 1 && STRLEN(?alt) = 1, "SNV",
    IF(STRLEN(?ref) = STRLEN(?alt), "MNV_OR_EQUAL_LENGTH_SUBSTITUTION",
    IF(STRLEN(?ref) < STRLEN(?alt), "INSERTION_SHAPE", "DELETION_SHAPE"))))))) AS ?variantClass)
}
GROUP BY ?variantClass
ORDER BY ?variantClass
