PREFIX gvo: <http://genome-variation.org/resource#>
PREFIX faldo: <http://biohackathon.org/resource/faldo#>
PREFIX dct: <http://purl.org/dc/terms/>
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
# TogoVar vcf2rdf v1.0.0-beta.12, run with --no-normalize so gvo:pos/ref/alt keep the VCF values.
# It writes one node per ALT allele and no node for the record, so records are regrouped on
# (reference, POS, REF, ID), all of which every allele node carries.
SELECT ?variantClass (COUNT(?record) AS ?recordCount)
WHERE {
  {
    SELECT ?record (SAMPLE(UCASE(STR(?refLiteral))) AS ?ref)
           (GROUP_CONCAT(UCASE(STR(?altLiteral)); separator=",") AS ?alt)
    WHERE {
    ?allele gvo:pos ?pos ; gvo:ref ?refLiteral ; dct:identifier ?id ;
            faldo:location/(faldo:reference|faldo:begin/faldo:reference) ?seq .
    BIND(CONCAT(STR(?seq), "|", STR(?pos), "|", STR(?refLiteral), "|", STR(?id)) AS ?record)
      ?allele gvo:alt ?altLiteral .
    }
    GROUP BY ?record
  }
  BIND(IF(?alt = ".", "NO_ALT", IF(CONTAINS(?alt, ","), "MULTIALLELIC",
    IF(?alt = "*" || CONTAINS(?alt, "[") || CONTAINS(?alt, "]") ||
       (STRSTARTS(?alt, "<") && STRENDS(?alt, ">")), "SYMBOLIC_OR_BREAKEND",
    IF(!REGEX(?ref, "^[ACGTN]+$") || !REGEX(?alt, "^[ACGTN]+$"), "OTHER",
    IF(STRLEN(?ref) = 1 && STRLEN(?alt) = 1, "SNV",
    IF(STRLEN(?ref) = STRLEN(?alt), "MNV_OR_EQUAL_LENGTH_SUBSTITUTION",
    IF(STRLEN(?ref) < STRLEN(?alt), "INSERTION_SHAPE", "DELETION_SHAPE"))))))) AS ?variantClass)
}
GROUP BY ?variantClass
ORDER BY ?variantClass

# "not filtered" to htsjdk). The port reads a record with no vcf:filter as PASS; a file whose

      OPTIONAL { ?record vcf:filter ?filterIri BIND(STRAFTER(STR(?filterIri), "urn:filter/") AS ?filterId) }
    }
    GROUP BY ?record

  BIND(IF(COALESCE(?filters, "") = "", "PASS", ?filters) AS ?filterLexical)
  BIND(IF(?filterLexical = "PASS", "PASS", "FAILED") AS ?filterStatus)
}
GROUP BY ?filterStatus ?filterLexical

PREFIX vcf: <http://github.com/lindenb/jvarkit/>
PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
# JVarkit vcf2rdf (commit fc2356a3), run with --hide '' so ALT, FILTER and GT are written.
# Its classes are written as IRIs with the scheme "vcf" (<vcf:Variant>), not as prefixed names,
# so they are matched literally. A record is <urn:variant/CHROM:POS:REF>.
# One <vcf:Genotype> per record and sample, typed by htsjdk's call class. A no-call carries no
# class and is read as MISSING; JVarkit writes no ploidy, so haploid calls cannot be told from
# homozygous ones.
SELECT ?sampleId ?genotypeClass (COUNT(DISTINCT ?genotype) AS ?callCount)
WHERE {
  ?genotype a <vcf:Genotype> ; vcf:sample ?sample .
  BIND(STRAFTER(STR(?sample), "urn:sample/") AS ?sampleId)
  OPTIONAL {
    ?genotype a ?class .
    VALUES (?class ?mapped) {
      (<vcf:HomRefGenotype> "HOM_REF") (<vcf:HomVarGenotype> "HOM_ALT")
      (<vcf:HetGenotype> "HET") (<vcf:HetNonRefGenotype> "HET")
    }
  }
  BIND(COALESCE(?mapped, "MISSING") AS ?genotypeClass)
}
GROUP BY ?sampleId ?genotypeClass
ORDER BY ?sampleId ?genotypeClass

PREFIX sg: <https://sparqling-genomics.org/0.99.11/>
PREFIX vc: <sg://0.99.11/vcf2rdf/>
PREFIX v: <sg://0.99.11/vcf2rdf/variant/>

PREFIX xsd: <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
# SPARQLing Genomics vcf2rdf 0.99.11, default options. It writes one vc:VariantCall per record and
# sample, and only for calls with a non-reference allele; there is no record node. Call IRIs are
# origin://<md5>@<k> with k = record index x samples + sample index (doc/command-line-tools.tex),
# so records are regrouped on floor(k / samples). Only the first ALT allele is written.
# Calls are written only when they carry a non-reference allele, so HOM_REF, HAPLOID_REF and
# fully missing calls are absent from the graph.

WHERE {
  ?call a vc:VariantCall ; sg:sample ?sample ; vc:ploidy ?ploidy ; gt:allele_1 ?a1 .
  ?sample rdfs:label ?label .
  OPTIONAL { ?call gt:allele_2 ?a2 }
  OPTIONAL { ?call gt:allele_3 ?a3 }
  BIND(STR(?label) AS ?sampleId)
  BIND(IF(?a1 < 0 || COALESCE(?a2, 0) < 0 || COALESCE(?a3, 0) < 0, "MISSING",
    IF(?ploidy >= 3, "OTHER_PLOIDY",
    IF(?ploidy = 1, IF(?a1 = 0, "HAPLOID_REF", "HAPLOID_ALT"),
    IF(?a1 = ?a2, IF(?a1 = 0, "HOM_REF", "HOM_ALT"), "HET")))) AS ?genotypeClass)
}
GROUP BY ?sampleId ?genotypeClass
ORDER BY ?sampleId ?genotypeClass

WHERE {

    SELECT ?record (SUM(?callAn) AS ?an) (SUM(?callAc) AS ?ac) (MAX(?callMax) AS ?maxAllele)
    WHERE {

# cyvcf2 arms (indexed seek or full scan, then START <= POS <= END)

A tabix/CSI seek returns every record whose span overlaps the region, so both indexed arms keep the seek and then drop records whose POS lies outside the window; the SPARQL side substitutes {{CHROM}}, {{START}} and {{END}} into the template (render_query, 698-713). Unlike q05 it starts from the record, because the coordinate restriction lives there. A record without a GT field prints '.' from bcftools and so classifies as MISSING there but NO_GT_FIELD on the cyvcf2 arms (documented in _classify_bcftools_gt); the comparator would flag it. The regional cyvcf2 readers are opened without strict_gt=True, unlike parse_vcf.

PREFIX vcfc: <https://w3id.org/vcf-core/vocab#>
PREFIX xsd:  <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>

# R5 - per-sample genotype classes inside one window.
#
# Unlike the whole-file q05, this starts from the record rather than the
# SampleCall, because the coordinate restriction lives on the record. The
# genotype classification below is identical to q05's.
SELECT ?sampleId ?genotypeClass (COUNT(DISTINCT ?sampleCall) AS ?callCount)
WHERE {
  ?record a vcfc:VCFRecord ; vcfc:chrom ?chrom ; vcfc:pos ?pos ; vcfc:hasCall ?call .
  FILTER(STR(?chrom) = "{{CHROM}}")
  FILTER(xsd:integer(?pos) >= {{START}} && xsd:integer(?pos) <= {{END}})
  ?call vcfc:hasSampleCall ?sampleCall .
  ?sampleCall vcfc:sampleId ?sampleId .
  OPTIONAL {
    ?sampleCall vcfc:hasFormatValue ?gtValueNode .
    FILTER(STRENDS(STR(?gtValueNode), "/fmt/GT"))
    ?gtValueNode vcfc:fieldValue ?gtLiteral .
  }
  BIND(IF(BOUND(?gtLiteral), REPLACE(STR(?gtLiteral), "[|]", "/"), "") AS ?gt)
  BIND(IF(!BOUND(?gtLiteral), "NO_GT_FIELD",
    IF(CONTAINS(?gt, "."), "MISSING",
      IF(REGEX(?gt, "^[0-9]+$"), IF(?gt = "0", "HAPLOID_REF", "HAPLOID_ALT"),
        IF(REGEX(?gt, "^[0-9]+/[0-9]+$"),
          IF(STRBEFORE(?gt, "/") = STRAFTER(?gt, "/"), IF(STRBEFORE(?gt, "/") = "0", "HOM_REF", "HOM_ALT"), "HET"),
          "OTHER_PLOIDY")))) AS ?genotypeClass)
}
GROUP BY ?sampleId ?genotypeClass
ORDER BY ?sampleId ?genotypeClass

def _classify_bcftools_gt(raw_gt: str) -> str:
    """Map a `%GT` string onto the same classes cyvcf2's oracle produces.

    `bcftools query` hands back the genotype as text, so this reproduces
    `classify_genotype` from the lexical form rather than from allele indices.
    A record with no GT field prints `.` here, which is indistinguishable from
    a missing call -- so a file whose records lack GT entirely would make this
    arm disagree with the cyvcf2 arms, and the comparator would catch it.
    """
    normalized = raw_gt.replace("|", "/")
    if normalized in ("", "."):
        return "MISSING"
    if "." in normalized:
        return "MISSING"
    parts = normalized.split("/")
    if len(parts) == 1:
        return "HAPLOID_REF" if parts[0] == "0" else "HAPLOID_ALT"
    if len(parts) == 2:
        if parts[0] == parts[1]:
            return "HOM_REF" if parts[0] == "0" else "HOM_ALT"
        return "HET"
    return "OTHER_PLOIDY"
